raw_response:
I am 64 years old, and I have farmed these 9 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. Last year I put 16 kg of nitrogen per mu on my cotton and got about 480 kg of seed cotton per mu. This year I will raise that to 20 kg of nitrogen per mu. I sat down with the soil test form the county extension office gave me two years ago — my phosphorus is still acceptable but potassium has dropped to about 100 ppm, which is low for cotton. I will apply 20 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. I will put all the phosphorus and potassium down as base fertilizer before sowing, and split the nitrogen: half at planting and half at first flower in mid-July. I keep a written record of my costs, and I know that pushing above 20 kg nitrogen does not pay back on my 9 mu, but I would rather apply a little too much than risk empty bolls in autumn.

I will plant the improved Bt variety I buy from the dealer. I stopped saving my own seed five years ago because the Bt trait weakens in the second generation, and the dealer gives me a reliable hybrid that costs about 55 yuan per mu. It is worth it — bollworm damage dropped sharply after I switched, and now I only spray 8 times per season: once at seedling stage for aphids, then every 10 to 12 days from early July to late August for spider mites and whitefly. Even with Bt cotton, the sucking pests still come hard. Each spray costs me about 22 yuan per mu for chemicals, plus my own labor. I do not hire anyone for spraying — at 64 I can still manage the tank on 9 mu.

For irrigation, I have my own tube well, but diesel is nearly 8 yuan per liter now. I will irrigate 3 times: once before sowing in late April to get the bed moist, once at first flower in early July, and once at peak boll filling in mid-August. I tried 4 times two years ago and the extra yield did not cover the diesel, so 3 times is the right balance for my land.

For tillage, I hire my nephew to bring his rotary tiller. It costs 50 yuan per mu and he finishes the 9 mu in one morning. Ploughing leaves big clods that make cotton planting difficult, and at my age I do not have the back for breaking them up by hand.

I expect 500 kg of seed cotton per mu this year. Last year I got 480, the weather forecast looks normal, and my neighbor Wang got 510 with the same variety. At the current price of 4.2 yuan per jin, that gives me about 9,450 yuan per mu gross. After paying for fertilizer, seed, pesticide, diesel, tillage, and the hired pickers I will need in September and October because there are only two of us in the household, I should clear enough to live on and keep some cash in case the well pump breaks again.
